findings.text: _in_flight_review catches every TypeError from the rule call to detect a one-argument stand-in, so a genuine TypeError raised inside recovery._review_in_flight's body is answered by a retry that re-reads the live directory and can return a different, quieter answer than the faulted call, which contradicts the docstring's claim at obligations.py:418-421 that 'a failure raised inside the rule's body raises again on the retry and surfaces from here'. Inspecting the signature before the call, or catching TypeError only around the keyword-bind, would keep the stand-in support without swallowing a fault.
